claims.text: An active-learning MLIP framework with targeted ab initio corrections can reduce the cost of evaluating absolute free energies for fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed framework can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
On-the-fly active learning will selectively invoke ab initio calculations in regions of high free-energy sensitivity.
Quasi-harmonic and anharmonic corrections will capture vibrational and electron–vibration effects.
The method will efficiently map solid- and liquid-phase free-energy surfaces.
The intended operating range is approximately 0.9 to 1.2 times the melting temperature at ambient pressure.
Electronic and lattice-dynamical effects play a pronounced role in phase stability over the proposed temperature range.
Periodic correction with targeted ab initio snapshots will accurately retain structural motifs controlling anharmonic and electron–vibration interactions.
Replacing continuous expensive ab initio molecular dynamics with selectively refined ML-driven sampling will accelerate free-energy evaluation.
Selective ab initio refinement will preserve all relevant entropic contributions to solid and liquid phase free energies.
The method will be 5 to 20 times faster than full ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
For elemental and binary systems, the method will achieve fidelity comparable to TOR-TILD.
The method will scale better than TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Previous explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD studies have reliably predicted phase-transition temperatures in elemental and binary systems.
The method is expected to perform robustly for systems containing up to several components near their melting conditions.
Application at extreme pressures or above 1.2 times the melting temperature may require additional validation because of limitations in representing complex electron–vibration coupling.
Accuracy depends on the quality and representativeness of the training data and active-learning corrections.

The benchmark will compare solid–liquid free-energy differences, melting temperatures, latent heats, and vibrational densities of states against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD under identical conditions.
Failure to reproduce benchmark phase free energies within ±10% will falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to reproduce observed melting points or latent heats within accepted experimental uncertainties will falsify the hypothesis.
